newsitem.title: USA: First Commerce sees Q3 eps $0.71 to $0.73.
newsitem.headline: First Commerce sees Q3 eps $0.71 to $0.73.

text.p: First Commerce Corp said on Monday it expected to report fully diluted earnings per share of $0.71 to $0.73 in the third quarter, against $0.76 per share in the second quarter, after an increase in loan loss provisions.
The company said in a statment its provisions for loan losses was expected to grow to $12 million to $14 million in the third quarter, from $7.5 million in the second quarter.
First Commerce earned $0.66 per share in the third quarter last year.
The increase in loan loss provisions was driven by higher credit card net charge-offs in the quarter, the company said.
Net charge-offs were $6.7 million, or 0.51 percent of total loans in the second quarter and were expected to be about $8 million in the third quarter, it said.
Credit card net charge-offs were expected to be $5.5 million in the current quarter from $4.9 million in the second quarter.
First Commerce said its credit card quality was significantly stronger than national averages, while following the recent national trend towards higher charge-off levels.
"Commercial asset quality remains excellent, with net recoveries again this quarter," the company said.
Credit card fees were also growing at a 35 percent annualized rate in 1996, the company said.
Loan growth should also continue at an annualized rate of over 20 percent in the third quarter, with significant increases in indirect automobile, credit cards and commercial loans, the company said.
Net interest income was expected to grow at a 10 percent annualized rate, driven by loan growth, it said.
